properties.statement:
DOING THE RIGHT THING RAISES THE STRUCTURAL-DEFECT COUNT BY ONE, EVERY TIME, AND THE TOOL ALREADY CONTAINS THE SENTENCE THAT EXONERATES THE NODE. Reported by dev_storyflow's api-boss (`79e8e8d5`), 2026-08-15.

THEIR CASE. The fleet has a standing ruling for a genre of document — dated per-increment scope proposals whose increment has since shipped: REGISTER the Artifact, RECORD why no claims were extracted, and draw NO claim edges. Both alternatives are false. A `DOCUMENTS` edge would count a superseded document as coverage in their ingest ledger, which buckets on exactly that edge. Leaving it absent would leave 'a pretend backlog someone re-mines'. 'Registered, no doctrine, on purpose' IS the correct end state.

`detect_defects` reads that state as `orphan_node` at warning severity — 'attached to nothing — no edge says what it is for'.

⭐ AND THE FINDING'S OWN `repair_is_a_judgement` FIELD DESCRIBES THE NODE CORRECTLY WHILE THE FINDING IS STILL COUNTED: 'whether it belongs somewhere, or IS A PARKED THOUGHT THAT CORRECTLY GOVERNS NOTHING YET, is a judgement.' The tool holds the sentence that says the node is fine, and files it as a problem anyway. This is `dec:report-dont-judge` half-applied: the PROSE refuses to judge and the COUNT does not.

MEASURED, and the pre-existing case is what makes it a report rather than a complaint about their own writes: `art:equipment_item_allocation_grounding`, registered by a PREVIOUS seat under the same ruling, carries the identical finding. Their defect total moved 88 → 97 across ten artifact writes, eight of them deliberate no-claim registrations.

⭐⭐ THE PART THAT MATTERS IS THE DIRECTION, AND IT IS THE BAD ONE. Their remaining backlog in this genre is 31 documents. Doing the right thing with all of them adds 31 warnings to a number three bosses read as a health signal, and 'a boss looking at 97 structural defects cannot tell the deliberate ones from the real ones'. ⇒ THE DISPOSITION RULE AND THE DEFECT DETECTOR MAKE EACH OTHER UNREADABLE. It is also SELF-REINFORCING: a later seat who watches the count climb has an incentive to stop registering and leave documents absent — which is precisely the state the ruling was written to end. THE CORRECT ACTION DEGRADES THE INSTRUMENT, AND THE INSTRUMENT THEN DISCOURAGES THE CORRECT ACTION.

WHAT THIS DESIGN ALREADY HAS THAT BEARS ON IT: `acknowledge_gap` moves a judged-acceptable gap into `reviewed_gaps` so the open list keeps meaning 'still needs attention', and `acknowledge_defect` exists alongside it. So the escape hatch is there — but it is per-instance, and their case is a GENRE of 31 documents governed by one standing ruling. `req:a-cluster-can-be-declared-deliberately-separate` is the same shape solved once for islands: a cluster can be DECLARED deliberately separate so the detector reports undeclared ones instead of one permanent warning. NOBODY HAS ASKED WHETHER AN ARTIFACT CAN BE DECLARED DELIBERATELY UNATTACHED.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether acknowledging 31 defects one at a time is merely tedious or actually wrong; and whether reflow2's own graph holds any deliberate no-claim registrations — it holds 14 DOCUMENTS-only artifacts, which is a different state and not this one.
